# Sirach Chapter 29 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 29 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**29:1** One who shows mercy will lend to his neighbor, and one who strengthens him with his hand keeps the commandments.

**29:2** Lend to your neighbor in the time of his need, and in turn pay back your neighbor at the appointed time.

**29:3** Keep your word and deal faithfully with him, and at all times you will find what you need.

**29:4** Many have treated a loan as a windfall, and brought grief to those who helped them.

**29:5** Until he receives the money he kisses his neighbor's hands and speaks humbly about his neighbor's money; but when repayment time comes he postpones, returns words of complaint, and blames the circumstances.

**29:6** If he can manage it, he will barely repay half and count it as a windfall; if not, he will rob him of his money and make an enemy of him for nothing. He repays him with insults and abuse, and in place of honor repays him with dishonor.

**29:7** Many have refused to lend — not from wickedness — because they feared being wronged without cause.

**29:8** Nevertheless, be patient with one who is in humble circumstances, and do not make him wait for your alms.

**29:9** For the sake of the commandment help the poor, and according to his need do not send him away empty.

**29:10** Spend your silver for a brother and a friend, and do not let it rust away under a stone and be lost.

**29:11** Lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High, and it will profit you more than gold.

**29:12** Lock away almsgiving in your storerooms, and it will deliver you from every evil.

**29:13** More than a mighty shield and more than a heavy spear, it will fight on your behalf against your enemy.

**29:14** A good man will stand surety for his neighbor, but one who has lost his sense of shame will abandon him.

**29:15** Do not forget the kindness of your guarantor, for he has given his life for you.

**29:16** The sinner will ruin the goods of his guarantor,

**29:17** and the ungrateful person will abandon the one who rescued him.

**29:18** Standing surety has ruined many who were prosperous and shaken them like a wave of the sea; powerful men have it made to wander, and they have wandered among foreign nations.

**29:19** A sinner who goes surety and undertakes contracts will fall into lawsuits.

**29:20** Help your neighbor as you are able, and take heed to yourself that you do not fall.

**29:21** The necessities of life are water and bread, clothing and a house to cover one's nakedness.

**29:22** Better is the life of a poor man under a shelter of logs than sumptuous fare in the house of a stranger.

**29:23** With little or with much, be content; and you will not hear the reproach of living as a stranger.

**29:24** It is a miserable life to go from house to house, and where you are a stranger you dare not open your mouth.

**29:25** You play the host and pour out drink without thanks; and on top of it all you hear bitter words:

**29:26** "Come here, stranger, set the table, and if you have anything on hand, feed me."

**29:27** "Get away, stranger, before an honored guest — a guest has come; my brother is here and I need the place."

**29:28** Hard it is for a good-natured man — reproach about coming and going, lending and moneylending.
